title: John Snow and the Broad Street cholera outbreak
summary: A cholera outbreak began in Soho, London, on 31 August 1854 and killed about 500 people in ten days. John Snow plotted the cases from the addresses of the dead and traced them to a pump on Broad Street, now Broadwick Street. Local authorities agreed to remove its handle, and the outbreak subsided.

uncertainty.note: Start is the first day of the Soho outbreak. The pages opened do not give the day the pump handle was removed, so the end is recorded only as 1854.

as_recorded.value: A third outbreak began in Soho on 31 August 1854.
a violent and sudden outbreak emerged on 31 August 1854

where.historical_name: Broad Street, Soho, London, United Kingdom

importance.justification: A founding case of epidemiology, in which mapping cases pointed to contaminated water as the source of cholera.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the death toll: the London Museum says 500 died in 10 days, the Health Foundation says 127 died in the first 3 days; the summary uses the first and the figure is not a final count.
